thread:
maria: Heads-up — after landing the adaptive-batcher kernel-weighting tweak (PR: 0f1a2b3) we see a 12-18% tail latency regression on long-seqs in prod perf tests. nsys traces attached. Anyone looked at kernel-selection footprints yet?

kevin: I grabbed the nsys captures earlier. Kernel timeline looks different — we start seeing `matmul_fused_v2` used for more steps instead of `matmul_opt_v1`. That kernel has worse SM occupancy with our batch shape.

ashok: Can you paste the command you used to capture? I want to reproduce locally.

kevin: Sure — capturing with the lightweight sampling we used:  
```
nsys profile --output batchreg --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --stats=true --force
./bin/runtime --serve --config=tests/longseq_prof.yaml
```
I trimmed to the region around token generation start.

maria: The short repro is `python perf_repro.py --seq 2048 --batch 8 --model rwd-7b` — runs on latest can reproduce 3 runs out of 5.

olga: I compared before/after flamegraphs (links below). Before: flame://sha/0e4a; After: flame://sha/0f1a2b3 — you can see matmul hotspots shift at ~120ms offset. CPU timeline also shows increased spin in batcher-heuristic.

perf-ci: Automated bisect started. Current suspect range: a8c9..0f1a. Will post bisect results when finished.

ashok: I pulled a local patch that forces kernel selector to prefer `matmul_opt_v1` for seq>1024. Quick hack: set env KERNEL_SELECTOR_OVERRIDES=\"matmul=opt_v1:threshold=1024\" — with that the tail drops back to baseline. Not a fix but confirms selector change is the cause.

kevin: Nice. So kernel-weighting math in selector_probs.cpp changed how fallback costs are computed. The new weighting favors fused kernels for medium batch shapes; for long seq it misestimates internal memory traffic and picks the wrong kernel.

maria: Any idea which commit touched selector_probs? PR link?

ashok: PR was 0f1a2b3 — main change in selector_probs: replaced empirical cost model with weighted heuristics that include a new compile_penalty term. The penalty seems to overweight smaller latencies causing the fused kernel to look cheaper.

kevin: I ran `nvprof --analysis-metrics` on matmul calls. For fused kernel: higher L2 read/write and increased register spilling when seq>1024. For opt_v1: better sustained throughput. So weight calc is definitely off.

maria: perf-ci bisect finished: culprit commit is 0f1a2b3, bisect log: `first bad: 0f1a2b3`, `good: a8c9d4`.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-02-14T09:12 rolled PR 0f1a2b3 to staging (tag: staging-20260214-09).

olga: Proposed quick mitigation: revert selector weighting change for the short term and add unit regression test that runs kernel selector decision matrix across seq/batch shapes. Also suggest we add an nsys smoke that asserts kernel choice for long sequences.

kevin: Agreed. I can craft a minimal patch that clamps compile_penalty to a small epsilon for now. Patch snippet:  
```
// selector_probs.cpp
double compile_penalty = std::max(1e-6, cfg.compile_penalty);
score += compile_penalty * compile_cost;
```
That brings decisions back inline.

ashok: If we're going to revert, let's also add a perftest: `tests/selector_regressions/longseq_kernel_choice.py` that asserts the selector picks `matmul_opt_v1` for seq>=1024,batch<=8.

maria: Who wants to own the revert + test? Need it in staging today.

kevin: I'll open a revert PR and include the test + an nsys capture artifact. Assign to me.

maria: Thanks. After revert, let's follow up with a longer-term fix: improve the cost model sampling (measure real mem traffic at candidate shapes) instead of heuristics. Add to roadmap.

kevin: Uploading trimmed nsys files and side-by-side perf logs to the thread: /artifacts/nsys/1765032000/before.nsys /artifacts/nsys/1765032000/after.nsys and perf summaries: /artifacts/perf/1765032000/before.txt /artifacts/perf/1765032000/after.txt

olga: I'll own the regression test and hook it into CI perf-smoke so we don't regress again silently.

perf-ci: CI job `selector_regression` queued — will run on staging once revert merges.

maria: Great. Once revert is merged, please post the staging perf numbers here and mark this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Revert PR opened: https://git.company/infra/runtime/pull/4123 — includes test and nsys artifacts.

ashok: Reviewed + approved. Merging after perf-ci passes.

deploy-bot: Deploy to staging scheduled: staging-rollback-1765032000 (eta 10m).

maria: Closing loop — staging perf after revert: tail p99 down 14%, median unchanged. Will monitor prod roll. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
